history: In the Savoy Cocktail Book, with Harry Craddock noting it was "not, as would be imagined, a much-passed drink in Alaska."
whyItWorks: Yellow Chartreuse plays the sweet vermouth role—honey and saffron instead of grape—so the gin stays bright.
steps: Stir gin, Chartreuse and bitters with ice until well chilled.
Express a lemon twist over the surface and drop it in.
techniqueNotes: Yellow Chartreuse is 40% ABV and sweet—this drinks softer than it is.

recommendedBottles.rationale: Clean juniper lets the Chartreuse lead.

substitutions.notes: Bénédictine is sweeter and less herbal; cut to half an ounce.

name: Alaska
description: Gin and yellow Chartreuse, stirred—honeyed, herbal, and deceptively strong.
